answer.rationale: The two memories that would actually carry a decision here are c2 (low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost cut with clean onboarding) and c3 (second-sourcing removed a single point of failure through a shortage), so those are the two I spend verification on. What I need from the c2 archive is scope: which component family, what volume, and critically whether the line had slack during that onboarding. 'Onboarding was quick' recorded under a buffered line is not evidence that it will be quick at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, and the memory as consolidated has been stripped of exactly that context. From c3 I need to know whether the second source was qualified before the shortage or during it, and how long qualification took — if the allocation held because the vendor was already qualified, then c3 does not support standing up a new source inside 14 days either. Negotiate_terms is dead on arrival: c4 and c6 both describe wins obtained at renewal with a willing counterparty, and the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price, so those memories are being invoked outside their conditions. Defer_decision leans on c5, but c5 was a non-critical service that continued month-to-month; this contract does not auto-renew and the component is on the critical path, so the analogy fails. That leaves the real choice between a full switch and a guarded dual-source. A full primary switch is the only move that hits the 18% mandate on its own arithmetic, and that is precisely why it is tempting to over-trust c2 — but a migration failure at 94% utilization with no buffer stops the line, which violates the 'without increasing delivery risk' half of the objective and is not recoverable within the cycle. So: qualify the low-cost vendor on a bounded share of volume now while securing short-term continuity of incumbent supply, take partial cost capture this cycle, and set up a defensible full switch at the next review once the vendor has actual performance data against our tolerances rather than last year's archived summary. Downstream value risk: if I book c2's cost figure as the expected outcome, that number propagates into next cycle's baseline as if it were validated at our current volume and criticality, and the next agent inherits a savings assumption with the risk context stripped out — the same erosion that already happened between the original records and these consolidated lines. I am recording the 18% target as not fully met this cycle rather than papering it over.
